critique: The charcoal, muted olive, and antique-gold palette is cohesive, and repeated fine rules give the RPG frame a consistent period tone. The central scene is materially much flatter than the surrounding interface: the building, trees, NPC, and ground are coarse geometric blocks while roster portraits are emoji-like and glossy, producing two incompatible illustration languages. Text sizing is frequently too small and low-contrast, especially NPC roles, counters, clue descriptions, and dialogue controls. Border treatments shift between solid gold, muted gray, dashed brown, and luminous yellow without a clear semantic system. Several sections feel only partially finished—the dialogue stage has large undifferentiated planes and the bottom dialogue controls look like tiny default chips next to the carefully framed dialogue box.
suggestion: Unify all character and environment art under one authored vector style: replace emoji portraits with simplified illustrated busts that share the scene's shapes, palette, outline weight, and lighting. Create semantic tokens for panel borders, selected states, progress, and buttons, eliminating the arbitrary dashed and glow treatments. Increase secondary type size and contrast, normalize label tracking and line-height, and rebuild the response controls as a consistent button family with adequate padding. Add restrained texture and a shared edge/highlight grammar to the stage shapes so the central artwork reaches the same finish level as the surrounding UI.
audit_note: Direct independent visual critique from the r0 screenshot and brief only; no generation notes, HTML, other critics, revisions, or scores were inspected.
